_note: Approved/limited_use snapshot only. Not the full research dataset. A phrase here is a candidate to consider when it fits the exact meaning, platform, audience and register of the copy you're writing — never insert it just because it's listed.

phrases.native_phrase: красивый шрифт для ника / красивые буквы
phrases.english_concept: beautiful/stylish font for a nickname or profile
phrases.usage_guidance: Primary head term for the RU generator/homepage and font-specific pages (krasivyy-shrift, generator-nikov); safe in titles/H1/meta.
phrases.good_example: Генератор шрифтов — красивые и стильные буквы

phrases.usage_guidance: Anchor term for symbol-library pages (special-characters, simvoly-discord, simvoly-roblox) and the nickname generator's symbol/frame sections.
phrases.good_example: Специальные символы — символы для ника, значки для копирования

phrases.usage_guidance: Use for the invisible/blank-name sections of symbol library and generator pages; pair with the concrete codepoint names (Hangul Filler, Braille Pattern Blank) the way ru/library/simvoly-roblox/index.html already does.
phrases.good_example: Невидимые и пустые имена для Roblox — используйте невидимый символ Hangul Filler

phrases.usage_guidance: Pairs with RU-003; use when describing the end result (blank-looking name) rather than the mechanism (the invisible character itself).
phrases.good_example: Невидимые и пустые имена для Roblox

phrases.usage_guidance: Primary head term for the RU bold-font page; the exact phrase people search alongside a platform name ('жирный шрифт вконтакте').
phrases.good_example: Работает ли жирный шрифт в Инстаграме, Телеграме, ВКонтакте и WhatsApp?

phrases.usage_guidance: Primary head term for the dedicated nickname-generator page; distinct from krasivyy-shrift (fonts) because it's framed around identity/naming, not letter styling.
phrases.good_example: Генератор ников ꧁꧂ — красивые ники для игр, копируй и вставляй

phrases.usage_guidance: Section header for the site's 'Ready-Made Names' pattern (per CLAUDE.md flair-engine notes) on generator-nikov and niki-standoff-2; keep the four-category split (крутые/тёмные/для девушек/короткие) that's already live.
phrases.good_example: Готовые ники — нажми, чтобы скопировать

phrases.usage_guidance: Label for the inline name-checker widget (game-rules.js initChecker); keep next to the input so users find it before spending in-game currency on a rename.
phrases.good_example: Проверка ника — обновляется, пока печатаешь

phrases.usage_guidance: Use in FAQ/trust-building copy that explains why UTG favors well-supported symbols; matches game-rules.js's own checker warning text.
phrases.good_example: На некоторых телефонах могут быть квадраты ▯

phrases.usage_guidance: Useful as an alternate/plain-language synonym for rendering-failure FAQ content, but note it's usually about charset mismatch (e.g. wrong file encoding), not specifically about missing Unicode glyph support like 'квадратики' — don't conflate the two causes in copy.
phrases.good_example: Кракозябры вместо русских букв — как исправить
phrases.avoid_when: do not use to describe the tofu-box/missing-glyph case (RU-010) — кракозябры specifically implies wrong-encoding garbage characters, a different failure mode from a rendered blank box

phrases.usage_guidance: Use verbatim — it mirrors the actual on-screen platform error text, which is why it's the searched phrase; already the anchor phrase in the Discord field-permissions guide.
phrases.good_example: Почему Discord пишет, что имя пользователя недопустимо?

phrases.usage_guidance: Pairs with RU-008 (проверка ника) as the risk being checked against — used in the site's own live checker copy.
phrases.good_example: Эта игра отклонит такой ник

phrases.usage_guidance: Use only in Standoff 2-specific content (e.g. the rename-instructions section) to explain why checking a name before renaming avoids wasted spend — this is the functional hook that makes RU-008's checker feature valuable.
phrases.good_example: На момент проверки смена ника стоит 500 голды
phrases.avoid_when: do not use outside Standoff 2 content, and never in a title/H1 — it is game-specific gamer slang, not a general term

phrases.usage_guidance: Use only as flavor copy on gaming ready-made-name sections aimed at competitive/'cool' name categories, not as a searchable head term.
phrases.good_example: Рамки, катакана и жирные буквы — для тех, кто тащит катки.
phrases.avoid_when: avoid in formal/explainer content or any non-gaming context; too niche-slangy for FAQ/meta

phrases.usage_guidance: Both 'VK' (Latin, current company/short branding) and 'ВКонтакте' (Cyrillic, classic full product name) are natural and already used interchangeably across ru/ pages depending on context — this is correct, not an inconsistency, given the 2021 rebrand kept both forms live in public use. The plain Cyrillic short form 'ВК' (as opposed to Latin 'VK') was not found in use anywhere on the RU site.
phrases.good_example: Работает ли жирный шрифт в Инстаграме, Телеграме, ВКонтакте и WhatsApp?

phrases.usage_guidance: Reserve for informal FAQ answers or example copy addressed casually to a younger audience; the site's existing formal title/meta usage ('Телеграм'/'Telegram') should not be replaced by this.
phrases.good_example: Кто-нибудь скинь стикеры в телегу
phrases.avoid_when: never use in title/H1/meta or any formal explainer copy — it reads as slang, not a platform name

phrases.usage_guidance: Same restriction as RU-017: informal-copy-only, never a title/meta replacement for 'Инстаграм'.
phrases.good_example: Залей это в инсту
phrases.avoid_when: never use in title/H1/meta or formal explainer copy

phrases.usage_guidance: This is the correct, formal RU translation already used site-wide to explain field-level Unicode support; keep it over the informal borrowed term 'юзернейм' in explainer content.
phrases.good_example: Имя пользователя против отображаемого имени: откуда берётся «недопустимое имя пользователя»

phrases.usage_guidance: Already the emotional close of the RU homepage's use-case card for game/profile names; keep it as the payoff line rather than a head term.
phrases.good_example: Добавьте стиля нику в игре или имени профиля. Просто скопируйте и вставьте — и вы уже выделяетесь.

phrases.native_phrase: уникальный ник / не как у всех
phrases.english_concept: wanting a unique nickname, not like everyone else's
phrases.usage_guidance: Good framing for a 'how to come up with a nickname' style intro section; distinct from RU-020 (the social payoff) in that this is about the origination/ideation step.
phrases.good_example: Как сделать уникальный никнейм?

phrases.native_phrase: имя для любимого / ник для парня в телефоне
phrases.english_concept: romantic pet-name for a partner's contact entry
phrases.usage_guidance: Relevant framing for a romantic/relationship-themed symbol or name-idea section (e.g. within library/serdechki or a heart-symbol ready-made-names block); combine with heart symbols (♥ ♡) already documented in library/serdechki.
phrases.good_example: ♥Александр♥

phrases.usage_guidance: Primary head term for the RU character-counter tool page; already well-optimized with platform-specific limit checks unique to the RU market (VK, Telegram, Cyrillic SMS).
phrases.good_example: Бесплатный счётчик символов и слов

phrases.english_concept: VK-specific character limits (wall post, status, message)
phrases.usage_guidance: A RU-market-specific data point not covered by English-language counters, which is the counter page's own stated differentiator — keep the exact numbers current if VK changes limits.
phrases.good_example: Запись на стене ВКонтакте вмещает около 15 940 символов, статус — 140 символов, а личное сообщение — до 4096 символов.

phrases.usage_guidance: A precise, differentiator-grade technical fact worth keeping in the counter page's FAQ; don't generalize the 70-char figure to non-SMS contexts.
phrases.good_example: SMS на кириллице вмещает в один сегмент всего 70 символов, а не 160, — потому что кириллица кодируется как UCS-2.

phrases.english_concept: a lettering tattoo (the tattooed inscription itself)
phrases.usage_guidance: This is the head concept for any Russian tattoo lettering surface. The pairing to use throughout is 'шрифт для надписи' — font for the inscription — which is exactly how Russian tool sites phrase it.
phrases.good_example: Шрифты для тату — подбери красивый шрифт для надписи онлайн.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use 'надпись' to mean a typeface. Outside tattoo context it means a sign/caption/label, so do not carry it onto the general Russian font pages.

phrases.native_phrase: тату-шрифты латинские — Ж, Щ, Ю, Я отсутствуют
phrases.english_concept: the Cyrillic problem — decorative tattoo fonts are Latin-only
phrases.register: informed-consumer / studio-explanatory; frustrated when a customer says it
phrases.usage_guidance: This is the single highest-value Russian angle. An honest FAQ that says which styles have real Cyrillic and which will fall back to plain letters answers a question Russian users are already asking. The site's own client-side Unicode approach has the same limitation and should say so plainly rather than imply otherwise.
phrases.good_example: Большинство красивых тату-шрифтов — латинские: буквы Ж, Щ, Ю, Я просто отсутствуют в оригинальном шрифте.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not claim the tool 'supports Cyrillic in all styles' unless it verifiably does — a Russian competitor makes exactly that claim and it is checkable. Keep this in FAQ/body, not in a title. Do not present the artist's hand-drawn workaround as a defect — Russian sources frame it neutrally.

phrases.native_phrase: в столбик / шапка профиля в столбик
phrases.english_concept: laying out a bio/profile description as a vertical column, one item per line
phrases.usage_guidance: Use 'в столбик' as the action phrase in the Russian stacked-text page title and FAQ ('Как сделать описание в столбик'), and 'шапка профиля' when referring to the Instagram bio field. Keep 'перенос строки' for the mechanism. Do not lead with 'вертикальный текст'.
phrases.good_example: Как сделать шапку профиля в Инстаграме в столбик — переносите каждую строку и вставляйте готовый текст.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use 'в столбик' for the ja/ko writing-mode sense. Do not use 'шапка профиля' for platforms where Russians do not call it that (it is Instagram-flavoured); on Discord/Telegram use the platform's own field name.

phrases.english_concept: 'emoji' in Russian — смайлик is still the everyday word, эмодзи the newer/precise one
phrases.register: 'смайлик' neutral and universal; 'эмодзи' neutral, younger/more precise
phrases.usage_guidance: Lead with the pair — 'Значения смайликов и эмодзи' — rather than choosing one, since the observed Russian editorial pattern (RBC Trends, Mamba) uses both together in the same headline. Use 'смайлик' when the referent is a face, 'эмодзи' when it is the full Unicode set.
phrases.good_example: Что означают смайлики и эмодзи: полный справочник с расшифровкой и значениями.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use 'смайлик' in Unicode/technical documentation — it is imprecise there. Do not use 'эмодзи' for the ASCII/parenthesis emoticons Russians actually type (see P23) — that is a different thing and conflating them loses the point.

phrases.english_concept: the closing-parenthesis smiley ')' '))' ')))' — a Russian-specific typed-emoticon convention
phrases.register: informal messaging/chat; extremely common across ages, but not written-formal
phrases.usage_guidance: This belongs on a Russian emoticon/emoji reference page as its own section — a Russian reader arriving at an 'emoticons' page expects the parentheses to be covered, and no machine-translated competitor page will have it. Explain the count-scales-intensity rule and the 'instead of a full stop' function. It is descriptive content about how Russians write, not a phrase to insert into UTG's own copy.
phrases.good_example: Что значат скобки в сообщениях? Одна ) — лёгкая улыбка, ))) — уже настоящий смех.
phrases.avoid_when: Never use ')' or ')))' in UltraTextGen's own Russian UI, button labels, or editorial voice — it would read as unprofessional from a brand. Do not describe it as universal: it is market-specific and the same characters mean nothing to a non-Russian reader. Do not carry it into pl/ua/other Slavic locale pages without their own evidence.

phrases.english_concept: text-built emoticons — the actual Russian head term
phrases.usage_guidance: Head a Russian kaomoji page with 'Смайлики из символов' and use 'каомодзи' as a section/category heading inside it (that is exactly the structure live Russian pages use). Do not make 'каомодзи' the H1 — it targets a much smaller, more specialist query.
phrases.good_example: Смайлики из символов — текстовые смайлы и каомодзи, которые можно скопировать в ник, Discord или Telegram.
phrases.avoid_when: Not appropriate as a technical term in copy about Unicode codepoints or rendering — there 'символы' alone is right. Do not use 'смайлики' when the page is specifically about the graphical emoji set.

phrases.english_concept: the Russian bracket smiley ')' / '))))' — and its generational register risk
phrases.register: informal; politeness marker; reads as 30+/'boomer' to Gen Z
phrases.content_surface: faq, body copy, culture/explainer sections — never the H1
phrases.usage_guidance: Excellent FAQ material on a Russian text-emoticon page ('Почему русские ставят скобки вместо смайлика?') — it is genuinely locally interesting, high-engagement, and something no machine-translated competitor page will have. Do NOT write UTG's own Russian marketing copy in this style: putting ')' at the end of the site's own sentences will date the brand to the audience segment that actually converts on gaming/aesthetic pages.
phrases.good_example: В русскоязычном интернете вместо ':)' часто ставят просто скобку — и чем больше скобочек, тем сильнее эмоция.
phrases.avoid_when: REGISTER WARNING — do not use ')' or ')))' in the site's own Russian voice on youth-facing surfaces (gaming nicknames, aesthetic/aльтушка, TikTok/Discord copy): it reads as an older person writing. It is fine, even friendly, in copy aimed at 30+ users. Never in technical, legal, or accessibility copy.

phrases.english_concept: ASCII art — the Russian technical vs. searched forms
phrases.register: neutral/technical for 'ASCII-графика'; casual for 'рисунки из символов'
phrases.usage_guidance: Use 'ASCII-арт' or 'рисунки из символов' in the H1 (matching how Russians search) and cite 'ASCII-графика' once as the proper term. Keeping the 'X из символов' pattern across the two surfaces ('смайлики из символов' / 'рисунки из символов') gives the Russian cluster an internally consistent, natively-shaped naming scheme.
phrases.good_example: Рисунки из символов (ASCII-графика) — картинки, собранные только из знаков клавиатуры.
phrases.avoid_when: Don't lead with 'ASCII-графика' — encyclopedic register. Don't use «эски» in copy at all; it's spoken jargon and will read as a typo.

phrases.usage_guidance: Use only to state the boundary in an FAQ. Frame it as a warning about behaviour, never as a feature.
phrases.good_example: Если вставлять один и тот же рисунок подряд, это воспринимается как копипаста-спам — в большинстве Discord-серверов за это выдают мут.
phrases.avoid_when: Never in a title, H1, meta or CTA; never in education/printables copy; never as a positive framing of what the generator produces.

phrases.english_concept: mojibake — the second native Russian word for garbled text, alongside кракозябры
phrases.register: neutral/help-desk; noticeably less playful than кракозябры
phrases.usage_guidance: Use иероглифы when the RU page needs a neutral, searchable troubleshooting heading; keep кракозябры (RU-011) for conversational body copy where the playful register fits. Do not use both in the same heading — that reads as keyword stacking.
phrases.good_example: Если вместо букв отображаются иероглифы, квадратики или вопросительные знаки
phrases.avoid_when: Never use иероглифы where the page is actually discussing CJK writing systems — the word literally means hieroglyphs and the collision is real and confusing on a site that also hosts CJK-adjacent symbol pages. Avoid in copy aimed at younger gaming audiences, where кракозябры is the live word.

phrases.english_concept: the umbrella verb for styling/decorating a username
phrases.usage_guidance: Confirms 'оформление' as the right umbrella word for hub-page titles/H1s across platform-specific RU pages, not a literal translation of 'decorate'.
Show both counts prominently on the RU page; 'б/п' is recognized shorthand. The 12-18% delta between modes is the money hook.
The diminutive сердечки — not сердца — is the searched form: сердечки символы 12,100/mo, and the live owner ru/library/serdechki is already slugged on it.
phrases.avoid_when: Use сердце in explanatory prose about the symbol itself; сердечки is the browse/collect register.
